findings.claim:
## Scope expansion: research → product + editorial/SEO
For every weekly finding classify as PRODUCT, CONTENT, BOTH, or WATCH/NO ACTION. Evaluate student usefulness, novelty, evidence, search intent, relevance to debt-free degrees, urgency and existing content overlap. Do not invent search volumes or keyword difficulty. Audit existing content and architecture before creating anything. For verified editorial opportunities, actually write or update substantive articles/guides/comparisons, not just a list of ideas. Include official citations, last verified date, accurate costs with assumptions, transfer and accreditation caveats, descriptive title/meta, canonical URL, appropriate internal links to verified pathways/tools, and applicable structured data/sitemap updates using existing conventions. Avoid thin or duplicative content, sensational claims, fake author expertise and publishing rumors as facts. Update existing pages when preferable; preserve URLs or redirects. Examples to independently verify: 90-credit bachelor's degrees; UMPI ACE policy changes; WGU $25 course eligibility and total costs; UMPI vs UMass MyPath; Purdue subscription pricing; Google certificate ACE validity; non-proctored college credit options. Content-only findings need not force product changes. BOTH findings should coordinate article and pathway releases so links and claims agree. Prepare actual content and product changes in a tested PR; publish via the established approved release workflow after verification and review, not by bypassing deployment safeguards. Track proposed/published URLs, status, evidence, and follow-up review dates. If Search Console/analytics are available, measure impressions, clicks, indexing and pathway engagement; do not fabricate metrics. Include this editorial triage in the permanent research intake workflow.
